situations: You praise a hotel to your friend: the receptionists, cleaners and cooks who work there are all friendly. Which noun means all these workers together?
A company has 200 employees. The boss says the group of people who work there will grow next year. Which word means 'staff'?
A restaurant sign says, 'Our team of waiters and cooks is happy to help.' You want the noun for the whole group of workers.

en: to occur, to come to mind, to remember, to collapse, to invade
situations: You stand in a shop and have no idea what to buy for your mother. Suddenly a good idea pops into your head.
You try to recall the name of your old teacher. After a minute it suddenly comes back to you. What do you do when a thought comes to your mind?
In a meeting nobody knows the answer, then a clever solution suddenly occurs to you. Which verb means 'to occur to someone'?
You park in a no-parking zone and find a paper under your windshield saying you must pay 30 euros.
A boy breaks a window while playing football. His parents take away his phone for a week so he learns his lesson.
The judge says the man must pay 500 euros for driving too fast. Which noun means 'punishment'?
You squeeze a banana at the market. It is soft, yellow and sweet, no longer green, and ready to eat.
Your 17-year-old cousin handles money and problems like a sensible adult, much more grown-up than most boys his age.
The tomatoes in the garden have turned red and can be picked now. Which adjective describes the fruit?
In a hospital you walk along a long, narrow passage with doors to many rooms on both sides.
At school the students wait in the long passage outside the classroom before the lesson starts.
Your hotel room is at the end of a long passage with identical doors in a row. Which noun means 'corridor'?
You open the door and see your best friend from abroad. Your heart fills with a big, happy feeling.
A girl gets a puppy for her birthday and jumps up and down with happiness.
You write on a card to a friend: 'Your visit gave us so much of this.' Which noun means 'joy'?
A bakery has twenty kinds of cake. You look at all of them and then pick one.
On a website you look at a seat map for your flight and pick the seat you like best.
Your boss shows you three photos and asks you to pick the best one for the poster. Which verb means 'to select'?
At driving school you first learn rules and road signs from a book, before you sit in a car. This part is not practice.
A scientist has an explanation for why the dinosaurs disappeared, but nobody has proved it yet.
Your friend says: 'It sounds easy in this, but in practice it is hard.' Which noun is the opposite of 'practice'?

en: on the one hand, for one thing
situations: You talk about moving to a big city. You name the first good point and know you will add the opposite point later. Which word means 'on the one hand'?
You think about buying a car: it is comfortable, but expensive. Which word starts your first point, before the second side?
You weigh two sides of a problem. Which word introduces the first side, 'on the one hand'?
A sign in the lift says no more than 8 people may ride at once. That is the highest allowed number.
You want the greatest possible effect, so you turn the volume knob to the very top.
Your teacher says you may take at most ten minutes for each question. Which word means 'maximum'?
A tree fell on your neighbor's car in the storm, and the roof is dented. You phone the insurance about it.
You drop your phone and the screen cracks. How big is the harm done?
The doctor warns that smoking does a lot of harm to your lungs. Which noun means 'damage'?
You do not know a word in your book, so you open your dictionary and search for it.
In the library you open a big encyclopedia to find facts about Berlin.
You are not sure how a word is spelled, so you check it in an online dictionary. What do you do?
You sit on the sofa and want to change the TV channel without getting up. You search between the cushions for the small device with buttons.
The TV will not switch on. Your dad says the batteries in the small device are empty.
Which noun means the 'remote control' that lets you change the TV from far away?
Newspapers, television, radio and the internet bring news to people. What are they called as a group?
A teacher shows students how to think carefully about what they read in newspapers and see on TV.
Reporters from many newspapers and TV channels wait outside the stadium for the coach. Which plural noun means 'media'?
At the post office the clerk puts your parcel on a scale to see how heavy it is.
You step on the bathroom scale to find out how many kilos you are.
At the vegetable stand the seller puts apples on the scale. Which verb means 'to weigh'?
You chop a round vegetable with many layers for the soup, and tears run down your face.
In autumn you plant small round things from the garden shop in the soil, and tulips grow from them in spring.
Your burger comes with tomato, cheese and rings of a sharp-smelling vegetable. Which noun is that vegetable?
Your neighbor helps old people with their shopping for free. She cares about others and the community.
A job at the city office is about helping poor families and people in difficult situations.
Which adjective describes anything that is about people living together in society?
A formal paper arrives from the city office in an envelope. It explains a new rule.
The school sends you an official written message about the parents' evening.
In an exam you must write a text with a pen. Along with reading, listening and speaking it is the fourth skill. Which noun means 'writing'?
On a sunny Sunday in the garden you put sausages and meat on a metal rack over hot coals.
Friends are coming for a party, so you buy charcoal for the device you cook meat on outdoors.
You say: 'Let's have a barbecue!' Which noun is the equipment you use for it?

en: to take care of, to make sure, to look after, to care
situations: Your sister goes on holiday and asks you to look after her cat. You promise to feed it every day.
Before the party the boss says: 'Please make sure there are enough drinks.' You say you will arrange it.
Parents work hard to provide food, clothes and a home for their children. Which verb means 'to take care'?
In the living room the floor is covered with a soft woven cover. Your cat sleeps on it, and you vacuum it every week.
In a shop in Turkey you admire a large hand-woven cover with colorful patterns for the floor.
You spill red wine on the floor covering in your hotel room, and the manager says it must be cleaned.
In the vote only 3 of 10 people said yes, so their group was smaller than the other group.
In a town a small group of people speak a different language from most of the people.
In your class 25 students are girls and 5 are boys. The boys are the smaller part. Which noun means 'minority'?
You have eaten one portion but are still hungry, so you ask the waiter for one more portion. Which adjective goes before the noun?
You already have one key, but the landlord gives you an extra one. Which adjective means 'additional'?
At the doctor you are asked if you have any other questions. Which adjective means 'further' or 'other'?
You see the floor is wet in the supermarket and tell a customer to be careful before she slips.
The radio tells people that a big storm is coming tonight, so they should stay at home.
Your friend wants to buy a car from a dishonest seller. You tell him not to, because you know the seller cheats.
A shop sign says the cheap price is only for this week, not normal. Which first part of a German compound noun means 'special' (as in a 'special offer')?
Football fans take an extra train that runs only on match day. Which word part means 'special' at the start of its name?
A bakery bakes a cake that is not on the usual menu, only for Christmas. Which prefix means 'special'?
You open your child's room: toys, clothes and books lie everywhere, all mixed up.
You drop your papers and they land on the floor in no order at all.
After the shocking news your thoughts are in a mess and you cannot think clearly. Which adverb describes this?
At a holiday camp the leader gives a program: swimming, hiking and games. Each item is something you can do in your free time.
A hotel offers yoga, tennis and a cooking class. Each item on the list is one of these.
The doctor says physical movement like daily walks is good for your heart. Which noun means 'activity'?
You work eight hours a day, five days a week, at the office, while your friend only works four hours a day.
A job ad says: 'We need a nurse for 40 hours per week, not part of the day.'
Your sister asks her boss to change from half days to all the working hours of a normal week. Which noun means 'full-time'?
You took photos on holiday and now send them from your computer to a website so others can see them.
Your teacher asks you to send your homework file to the school portal on the internet.
You made a video and put it on the internet platform so everyone can watch it. Which verb means 'to upload'?
It snows in your city in July. Nobody has ever seen this before.
Your friend wears green hair and a very strange hat. People stare because it is not what people normally do.
A restaurant serves ice cream with fish. It is strange and not common at all.
On a form you tick 'male' or 'female'. The box is labeled with this word.
At the doctor the ultrasound shows whether the baby is a boy or a girl. Which noun means 'sex' in this sense?
In your German class the teacher says every noun is masculine, feminine or neuter. Which noun names this property?
You hike up a mountain. From the top you look down at the low land between two hills, with a river and a village.
The village lies at the bottom between high mountains, and a river flows through it.
Which noun means the low land between two mountains?

en: to bump, to push, to encounter
situations: In a crowded bus you hit your head on the low door frame.
You walk in the dark and your foot hits the leg of the table. Which verb means 'to bump'?
During your research you come across a surprising old photo you did not expect to find.
Hundreds of students walk through the street with signs, shouting that they do not accept the higher bus prices.
You think a new rule is unfair, so you loudly say 'No!' in the meeting.
Neighbors collect names on a paper to show they are against a new road. Which noun means 'protest'?
At the park pond a bird with a flat beak swims and says 'quack'. Children throw bread to it.
At a Chinese restaurant you order a crispy roast bird with orange sauce, but it is not chicken.
A yellow rubber toy floats in the baby's bath. It is shaped like a bird that says 'quack'.
Your teacher explains grammar so simply that everyone in the class gets it.
The instructions for the machine are written in clear, easy words, so anyone can follow them.
Your friend lost his job and cries. You say you can easily see why he feels this way. Which adjective means 'understandable'?

en: to feel sorry for, to feel sorry about
situations: You accidentally step on a stranger's foot on the bus and want to say how bad you feel about it.
Your friend's grandfather died. You tell him you feel sad for him.
You arrive an hour late to a meeting and tell your boss you regret it. Which verb means 'to feel sorry'?
Your mother says angrily: 'You never help in the house!' She is blaming you for something.
A customer says the shop cheated him, and the owner denies it. This claim that someone did wrong is called what?
Your friend did not call for weeks. You tell him how disappointed you were, and it sounds like blame.
At the cash desk you pay with a paper note of 20 euros, not with coins.
You show your swimming teacher the paper that proves you passed the test.
In a dark room you see only the weak glow of a candle. Which noun means this light?
A small grey animal with a long tail runs across the kitchen floor, and the cat chases it.
Your laptop pad does not work, so you plug in a small device with two buttons and click with your hand.
In the cartoon a famous character with round ears and a squeaky voice is this animal.

en: to approve, to authorize, to authorise, to grant permission, to permit
situations: You asked your boss for two weeks of holiday. She signs the paper and says yes, it is allowed.
The city office checks your plan for a new garage and officially says you may build it.
Your bank accepts your request for a loan. Which verb means 'to approve'?
A parking sign says the fee applies on every normal working day, but not on Sundays.
Your gym offers a cheaper ticket that is only valid on working days.
A shop is open Monday to Saturday. Which adverb means 'on working days'?
Your friend is very sick. You believe she will get well soon, and you wish for it.
You wait for your exam results and wish with all your heart that you passed.
After months without work you got an interview. It gives you a good feeling that things may get better.
It rains hard on your wedding day, but you smile and say it will surely be fine later.
Your friend failed the exam but says the next time will be better. He always sees the bright side.
Which adjective describes a person who expects good things to happen?
At breakfast you pour hot coffee from a container with a handle and a spout into the cups.
In the garden you fill a metal container with water to water the flowers.
In a restaurant you ask for a big container of water for the table, and the waiter brings one made of glass with a handle.
You hold a key in the door lock and move it in a circle to open the door.
To make the radio louder you move the knob around to the right.
The big wheel at the fair slowly goes round and round. Which verb means 'to rotate'?
At the summer camp a young man looks after the children, plays with them and keeps them safe.
At a care home a man helps old people with eating and walking.
During your internship at a company, a man guides you and checks your work. What do you call him?
Two neighbors who argued for years finally shake hands. There is no more quarrel, and everything is calm.
Children draw a white dove at school and write a wish for a world without war.
Two countries sign an agreement to end a long conflict. Which noun means 'peace'?
You add the prices of all the items in your basket and see the final sum at the end.
The teacher says the entire class must stay after school, not only two students.
A company has 5000 workers in all its countries together. Which adjective means 'total' or 'whole'?
A salesman says the car has never had an accident, but you are not sure you can believe him.
You wonder if you chose the right job, and a small voice says maybe not.
The police have no uncertainty about who the thief is. Which noun means 'doubt'?
Children at the swimming pool run to the edge and push off with both feet into the water.
A frog moves quickly from one stone to another by pushing off with its legs.
In the gym the coach says: 'Leave the ground with both feet, again and again, to warm up.'
In the hospital ward a man lies in bed with a fever, and the nurse checks on him.
A volunteer visits a man who is too ill to leave his house and brings him food.
The doctor says a man who is ill should rest at home. What do you call the man?
A baby first crawls, then walks, then speaks. The doctor checks how the child is progressing.
A company creates new software over many months. This process of making something new is called what?
The news reports how prices have changed over the last ten years.

en: to break in, to cave in, to collapse
situations: Thieves get into a house at night through a window, and the police are called.
A heavy load of snow makes the old roof of the barn fall in.
A man walks on thin ice on a lake, and it breaks under him. Which verb means 'to cave in'?
At the zoo an animal with a very long neck eats leaves from the top of a tall tree.
In Africa lives a yellow animal with brown spots, the tallest animal in the world.
A child's drawing shows an animal that is taller than the house, with a neck like a tower.
The soup tastes too much of salt, and you drink a lot of water afterwards.
At the cinema you prefer crisps and peanuts over sweets, because you like this taste more.
Sea water has a strong taste. Which adjective describes it?
After school sixteen-year-old Anna works three years at a bakery and goes to vocational school to become a baker.
The story ends with a moral: do not lie. What the story teaches you is called what?
After the accident you learned something important for the future: always check the brakes.
You ask a colleague whether he has finished the report. He says it is done, even earlier than expected.
You arrive at 8 o'clock and your friend is there, since he came before you.
The teacher is surprised that you finished the test so early. Which adverb means 'already'?

en: to inquire, to ask, to make enquiries
situations: Before buying a ticket you go to the information desk and ask what time the train leaves.
You phone the hotel to find out whether they have a free room and what the price is.
A friend is in hospital, so you call to ask how he is. Which verb means 'to inquire'?
In the shop you look at two phones side by side and check price and battery.
The teacher gives you two poems and asks you to say how they are alike and how they are different.
A test magazine puts ten washing machines in a table and rates each one. What is this called?
On Sunday your family goes to a big park where you can see lions, monkeys and elephants.
On a school trip the children go to see animals from different countries in enclosures.
Which noun means a place where you can visit wild animals?
It is 3 pm, you skipped lunch, and your stomach is growling loudly.
After a long hike you would like a big plate of pasta because your belly is empty.
The baby is crying and wants milk. Which adjective describes how the baby feels?
Your grandfather tells stories about the time when he was small, played in the village and went to primary school.
In an interview someone says that in his early years they had no TV.
Which noun means the time of life before you are a teenager?
The driver realizes the car is going the wrong way and wants to turn it around.
You cook a pancake and flip it in the pan to cook the other side.
You finish a page of the book and move it over to read the next one. Which verb means 'to turn'?
Your teacher says to write notes in the white space beside the text on the page.
Be careful with the glass: do not fill it to the very top, up to the rim.
Do not stand so near the end of the cliff. Which noun means 'edge'?
At the old church a tall narrow part with bells rises above the roof, and you climb the stairs for the view.
In a medieval castle guards look out from a tall round building.
Paris is famous for a tall iron structure that is higher than all buildings. Which noun means 'tower'?

en: to suggest, to propose, to recommend
situations: Your friend does not know what to do on Saturday, and you say: 'Why don't we go to the cinema?'
In a meeting the team leader offers an idea for a new date for the event.
The waiter says you should try the fish soup. He is doing this.
You are unsure which job to choose and ask your uncle what you should do. He gives you this.
A friend gives you a useful tip: 'Learn ten words every day.'
Which noun means 'advice' as a single helpful suggestion?
You look for shoes for a long mountain hike, and sandals are not right for this.
The job needs a patient person, and you decide the candidate is a good match.
A hotel room for a family with four kids: a single room is not appropriate. Which adjective means 'suitable'?
At the theatre you hand over your coat and get a numbered tag. Which noun is the room where coats are kept?
In the hallway of the flat there is a place on the wall with hooks to hang jackets.
The actress has a huge collection of dresses and shoes, her whole set of clothes.
On the farm a big black-and-white animal gives milk every morning.
In the Swiss mountains large animals with bells around their necks eat grass on the meadow.
Your child asks which animal says 'moo'.

en: to consider, to think about, to deliberate
situations: The salesman wants an answer now, but you say you need time to think about the offer first.
Your friend asks if you will move to Berlin. You say you must weigh it carefully.
Before choosing a university you think for several days about the pros and cons. Which verb means 'to consider'?
At the office you put a paper in the machine and get a second identical sheet.
The office asks for a paper copy of your passport, so you go to the print shop.
A painting in the museum is not the original, but a replica of it.

en: just as, just the same, equally
situations: Your brother is 180 cm tall and you are 180 cm too. Which adverb means 'just as'?
You compare two phones. This one is exactly as expensive as the other. Which adverb means 'equally'?
A friend says she loves pizza, and you say you feel just the same.
Your teacher gives you ten grammar tasks to do at home so that you can practice.
At the gym the trainer shows a movement for your back that you repeat 15 times.
Pianists play scales every day. This repeated training is called what?
Twins look the same, but their characters are not the same at all. One is quiet and one is loud.
The prices in the shops are not the same. One costs 5 euros and another 9.
The weather in April keeps changing, sometimes sunny and sometimes rainy. Which adjective means 'variable' or 'different'?

en: to forgive, to excuse, to pardon
situations: Your friend forgot your birthday and says sorry. You say it is okay and you are not angry anymore.
You said something rude to your sister, and you ask her to let it go.
Someone bumps into you and says sorry, and you say no problem. Which verb means 'to forgive'?
The pyramids are about 4500 years old, which is several periods of one thousand years.
On New Year's Eve in 2000 people celebrated the start of a new period of one thousand years.
One thousand years make up one of these. Which noun means 'millennium'?
To hang a picture you hammer a small thin metal spike into the wall.
At the beauty salon you paint the hard plates at the tips of your fingers red.
In a carpenter's box you find screws and these. Which noun means 'nail'?
You sit on a bench in the park and quietly look at the birds to see what they do.
A scientist watches how plants grow every day and writes notes.
The teacher says: 'Look closely at the experiment and note what happens.'
In the city center you take an electric vehicle on rails along the street. It is not a bus and not an underground train.
In Vienna you buy a ticket for the street rail line that rolls through the city and rings a bell.
A yellow rail car passes your window every ten minutes and stops at the stop in the street.
You studied all night for an exam that was already cancelled, so all your work was for nothing.
Your friend says it makes no sense to wait for the bus because the last one already left.
Digging a hole and filling it again is a task with no purpose at all.
Your boss gives you a very difficult project that will test your skills, and you want to try.
Running a marathon on your first try is hard, but you like such tough tasks.
Learning German while working a full-time job is difficult. Which noun means 'challenge'?
If you do not wear a seat belt, a bad thing can happen as an effect. What do you call what follows from an action?
Last night you watched the new part of your favorite series on TV.
In math the numbers 2, 4, 6, 8 stand in a fixed order, one after another.
You feel a very strong dislike for getting up at five in the morning. It is the worst thing for you.
Your friend does not just dislike spinach, he feels very strong dislike for it. It is the opposite of loving.
Your brother cannot stand losing at cards. Which verb means 'to hate'?
After the business trip your boss wants a written summary of what you did.
The news on TV includes a short film and text about the flood in the north.
A student writes about her internship and lists everything in a paper for her teacher.
Near the river there is a big building with tall chimneys that makes the electricity for the city.
Water falls through big machines in a dam to create electricity.
A storm cuts off the power, and the company says the place that produces electricity has a fault.
Your old clock has hands, but the new one shows numbers on a screen.
The photos on your phone are stored as files, not as paper prints.
The company stops sending paper documents, and everything is now on computers.

en: to take off, to arrange an appointment, to agree
situations: You and your friend say 'let's meet at 5 pm at the station', and you both agree.
You peel the sticker off the bottle and take it away.
The boss and you settle on a price. Which verb means 'to agree on' something?
On the motorway a huge vehicle carries goods. It is much bigger than cars and loud.
A construction company brings sand to the building site in a heavy vehicle.
A driver delivers furniture over long distances in a big vehicle with a trailer.
The room is not hot or cold, just nicely warm. Which adverb describes the warmth?
The music was quiet and nice to listen to.
You expected a bad hotel but it was better than you thought, and you were happily surprised in a nice way.
You want to buy a novel as a present and walk into a shop with shelves of books on the high street.
On Saturday you go to a shop to buy school books.
Which noun means a place where you buy books, not borrow them?
The wedding party takes place in a big room with many tables at the hotel.
The concert is held in a large room with rows of seats.
The school play is in a large room with a stage.

en: to have in mind, to plan, to intend
situations: A friend asks about your plans for the weekend. You say what you have in mind: a trip to the lake.
You are going to take a course next year. It is your intention.
Which verb means that you have something in mind to do?
At 7 am construction machines work outside your window, and you cannot sleep.
In the classroom 30 children shout at the same time. It is very loud.
Your neighbors play loud music at midnight. Which noun means 'noise'?
Your internet does not work, and the hotline says another department is in charge of this problem.
At the town hall you ask which office is the right one for a new passport.
The boss asks who is responsible for the printer. Which adjective means 'responsible'?
The teacher says your essay has no clear order: introduction, middle and end are missing.
Scientists study how the atoms in a crystal are arranged.
A company changes how its departments and managers are organized.

en: to catch a cold, to catch a chill
situations: You went out in the rain without a jacket. The next morning you sneeze and have a runny nose.
Your child sat in the cold wind and now has a cough.
The doctor says: 'Dress warm so you don't get a cold.'
A spoon, a key and a coin are all made from this hard shiny material.
A magnet sticks to the fridge door because it is made of this.
Iron, copper and gold belong to this group of materials.
You broke the vase, and your sister says: 'It is your fault.'
You owe the bank 5000 euros that you have not repaid yet.
You feel bad after lying to a friend. You have a heavy feeling of having done wrong.
In winter the lake ice is hard enough to walk on. It is no longer liquid. Which adjective describes it?
The teacher says the date of the exam is decided and will not change.
You hold the rope tightly and nothing can pull it out of your hands. Your grip is strong and does not give way.

en: to occupy, to fill, to man, to trim, to staff
situations: You put your jacket on a train seat so nobody else can sit there. What are you doing to the seat?
A company needs to find someone for its empty manager position. What must it do with the job?
The hospital needs enough nurses so the night shift has people at every desk. Which verb means 'to man' or 'to staff'?
In Berlin you go down the stairs into a station below the street, and a train arrives in a tunnel.
You want to avoid the traffic jams in the big city, so you take the train that runs under the ground.
London has the 'Tube' and New York has the 'Subway'. Which noun means this kind of train?
A woman from a country in danger arrives in Germany and asks for protection and a safe place to live.
A man has to leave his home country and applies for official protection in another country.
Which noun means the protection a country gives to people who flee from danger?
Every autumn birds fly in large groups to warmer countries and return in spring. Which noun names this movement?
Many people move from the countryside to big cities to find work.
The news reports that many people leave one country to settle in another.

en: to set, to define, to specify, to determine, to fix
situations: You and your landlord write exactly how much the rent will be in the contract. The amount is now decided.
The manager writes down the rules for the team: how long each break lasts.
The class agrees on a date for the trip, and everyone says it is final.
Your sister is expecting a baby, and the doctor says it takes about nine months.
A woman at work tells her boss she is expecting a child and will go on leave later.
In the pharmacy you buy a test to find out if a woman is going to have a baby.
A friend asks if you have seen a good film lately. You say you saw one just a few days ago.
You met your neighbor not long ago, and he told you he was moving.
You say you started your new job only a short time ago. Which adverb means 'recently'?
You taste the soup and it is the best you ever had. You tell the cook it is perfect.
A teacher reads your essay and gives you the best possible grade for superb work.
At the hotel the service was so good that you write a review with the highest praise.
On a form you must write your name, address and date of birth. These details are required.
The police ask you to tell them what you saw. What you tell them is recorded.
The label on the box shows the size and weight of the product. These facts are printed there.
The seller promises that if the phone breaks within two years, he will fix it for free.
The airline says you will get your money back for sure if your flight is cancelled.
Your friend says: 'I promise one hundred percent that I will be there at eight.'
In a block of flats you live on the third level above the ground floor, and you take the lift.
In the department store a sign says the toys are on the second level.
A hotel receptionist says: 'Your room is on the fifth level.' Which noun means 'floor' in a building?
The firefighters study why the fire started. They look for what made it happen.
The doctor wants to know what made you sick, so he asks about your food and your travels.
The train is late, and the announcer explains the reason: a fault with a signal.
The shop has only a tiny number of apples left. The amount is very small.
The doctor says the risk is very low, so you need not worry.
The difference in price between the two phones is only slight, just two euros.
A new family from abroad learns the language, goes to the local school and makes friends. They become part of the community.
The city offers language courses to help newcomers become part of society.
Which noun means the process of becoming a full part of a group or society?
A stamp must be put on the envelope with a bit of gum.
Your child makes a paper picture and attaches little pieces with paste.
The sticker will not come off. It stays on the window. Which verb means 'to stick'?
Your jacket has small round pieces that go through holes to close it, and one has fallen off.
To call the lift you push a round thing on the wall.
The radio has a round thing you turn to make the sound louder.
A boy breaks his arm at night. His parents drive to the part of the hospital that is open all day and night for urgent cases.
Your friend has strong chest pain on Sunday and no doctor's office is open, so you go to a special hospital department.
A hospital sign says: 'Open day and night for serious accidents.'

en: to break, to bust, to destroy
situations: A toddler pulls the toy so hard that it is ruined. You say: 'You have ruined it!'
Your brother dropped your phone, and now it does not work anymore.
You step on your glasses by accident, and they are in pieces.
You hear a sudden loud bang behind you and your heart jumps.
Your friend jumps out from behind the door and you get a big scare.
You think you have lost your wallet, and a sudden feeling of fear goes through you.
The museum shows the real painting by the artist, not a copy.
A shop sells genuine brand shoes, not fake ones.
You watch a film in the language it was first made in, not dubbed.
At ten o'clock all colleagues sit around a table in the office to talk about the project.
Your boss says: 'I cannot talk now, I am in a work discussion with the team.'

A magazine story ends with 'To be continued next week.' You wait for the next part.
The meeting stops at noon, and the rest will go on tomorrow morning. Which word means 'continuation'?
The doctor says your appendix must be removed. You will sleep under anesthesia while a surgeon cuts and fixes it.
Your grandfather's hip is being fixed in the hospital, and you wait for three hours with the family.
Your friend broke a bone badly and needs surgery. Which word means 'operation'?
You hold a hammer in your hand. Your friend asks what you plan to do with it. Which small word means 'with it'?
Your friend gives you a fragile gift and says: 'Be careful ___!' Which word means 'with that'?
A technician points at a broken machine and asks if you know how to work with it. Which small word means 'with that'?

en: to change, to alter, to modify
situations: Your hairdresser cuts your long hair very short. You look completely different from before.
After moving to a new city, you notice your habits are not the same as before. The city made you different.
You open the design file and make small adjustments to the colors. Which verb means 'to alter'?
At the football match there were so many fans that the stadium was completely full, a huge number of people.
The bookshop has hundreds of cookbooks on its shelves, a great many.
The teacher says the students sent a large number of questions after the lesson. Which adjective means 'numerous'?
In many countries, every child must go to school. It is not a choice, because the law says you have to.
As a lifeguard, you have to watch the swimmers. It is part of your job, and you cannot skip it.
Voting is a right, but paying taxes is something you must do. Which word means 'duty'?
After two years abroad, your sister comes back home next week. The family prepares a welcome party for her arrival.
The astronauts' journey back from space to Earth was successful.
The travel plan says: 'Day 7: going back to the place where we started.' Which word means 'return'?

en: to dismiss, to fire, to lay off, to release
situations: The company has no money left. The boss tells fifty workers that they must leave their jobs and will not be paid any more.
After a week in hospital, the doctor says you may go home today.
The boss is angry because Tom is late every day. He tells him to leave and not come back. Which verb means 'to fire'?
You cut your finger with a knife and a red liquid comes out. You press a tissue on it.
At the doctor's, a nurse puts a needle in your arm to take a sample for a test.
A campaign asks healthy people to donate the red liquid that flows in the veins to help patients. What is it called?

en: object of addiction, addictive substance, addictive drug
situations: A health leaflet warns about alcohol, nicotine and drugs that people can become dependent on.
A doctor tells a patient to stay away from anything that can make a person addicted, like tobacco.
At school, a talk is about substances that can lead to dependence. Which word means 'addictive substance'?
A car has no petrol engine. It runs on a battery that you charge at a socket.
A sign on a fence says that power runs through the wire and touching it hurts.
Your toothbrush works with a battery and vibrates by itself. Which adjective means 'electric'?

en: to be, to be located, to be situated, to feel
situations: A friend calls: 'Where are you right now?' You answer, in a formal way, that you are currently at the airport.
After the operation, the nurse politely asks how you feel. You answer that you feel fine.
The museum guide says the old paintings are located in the east wing. Which verb means 'to be located'?
On a cold winter morning a child drinks something warm and sweet made of milk and chocolate powder.
The baker's recipe uses a brown powder that gives chocolate its taste.
At the café the kids order a warm chocolate drink with milk. Which word means 'hot chocolate' or 'cocoa'?
A small town has twelve thousand people living in it. A man who lives there is, for the town, one of these.
The mayor speaks to the people who live in the village, to every man who lives there.
The statistics office counts how many people live in Berlin. Which word means a male 'inhabitant'?
You fall off your bike and the skin on your knee is open and red. You clean it and put a plaster on it.
The nurse changes the bandage on the cut where the surgeon worked.
A football player has an open cut above his eye after a hard knock. Which word means 'wound'?
You tell your friend some surprising news, and you watch how he answers with his face and words.
You email your landlord about the broken heater, but he never answers. You wonder why he does not respond.
A driver sees a child run into the street and brakes immediately. He had to act fast. Which verb means 'to react'?
The parking lot has only twenty places for hundreds of visitors, so space is not unlimited.
A sign says only ten people may enter the room at the same time. The number is restricted.
You have only fifty euros for the whole month, so your money can only go so far. Which adjective means 'limited'?
Your friend tells you something personal and asks you not to tell anyone. You promise.
In a detective story nobody knows why the door was locked from the inside. Something remains unexplained.
At a surprise party the guests hide the plan from the birthday girl. Which word means 'secret'?
An old man of 70 pays a cheaper price at the museum because of his age.
A club for retired people offers chess and coffee afternoons. A man who is 72 joins it.
At the pharmacy, an advert offers a free health check for people over 65. Which word means a male 'senior citizen'?
A shop assistant asks if you need help. You answer politely that you are only looking, nothing more.
You say the repair cost just ten euros, nothing more. Which small word means 'only'?
Your friend ate a tiny piece of cake and says it was simply a taste. Which little word means 'just'?
You walk behind your guide through the forest, staying close and going where she goes.
On your phone you see a friend's posts every day because you subscribed to her account.
The teacher speaks so fast that you cannot keep up with her explanation as it goes along. Which verb means 'to follow'?
At the farm, potatoes are packed in a big, rough bag that holds many kilos.
Father Christmas carries the toys on his back in a big cloth bag.
You buy cement. It is sold in a heavy paper bag of 25 kilos. Which word means 'sack'?
You ask the waiter which dish is the best. He suggests the fish soup.
Your old boss writes a letter for your new job application saying you are a good worker.
A friend tells you about a great film you should see. She gives you a tip. Which word means 'recommendation'?
A man stands next to a car at night and looks into every window. The neighbours think he may be up to no good.
A bag lies alone in the station and nobody knows whose it is. It looks strange.
You get an email from an unknown sender asking for your bank password. It looks like a trick. Which adjective means 'suspicious'?
On a newspaper page, big bold letters at the top tell you what the article is about.
When writing an essay, you put a short line in large letters above the first paragraph.
The teacher says each section of your homework needs a short name at the top. Which word means 'heading'?
Your neighbour wants to throw away a good chair. You say: 'Wait, I could put that to good use in my room.'
You read the instructions that explain how a drill is handled to make holes in the wall.
A friend gives you old clothes, and you say you can really find a purpose for them. Which verb means 'to use'?
At school you learn English, French or Spanish besides your mother tongue.
A job ad says that knowledge of at least one language other than your own is required.
In Bangladesh, students study Bengali as their own language and English as a second one from abroad. Which word means 'foreign language'?

en: continuing education, further education, further training
situations: You have worked as an accountant for ten years. Now you attend evening courses to learn new software and improve your skills for your job.
Your boss pays for a weekend seminar to help you grow in your profession.
A flyer offers courses for adults who already work and want to learn more. Which word means 'further training'?
A child falls into the river and a passer-by jumps in and pulls him out, so he does not drown.
Your laptop is dying, but you manage to keep your thesis from being lost just in time.
Firefighters carry people out of a burning house. Which verb means 'to rescue'?
The film critic writes a review that points out many weaknesses of the new movie.
The doctor says the patient's condition is serious and could become dangerous in the next hours.
A student does not simply believe everything in the news and checks the facts carefully. Which adjective describes this attitude: 'critical'?
Between your favourite TV show, short films try to make you buy a new shampoo.
Your mailbox is full of colourful papers offering cheap pizza and furniture.
A big poster at the bus stop shows a car and a slogan. Which word means 'advertising'?
You sign up for the city marathon. The form says that taking part costs 20 euros.
The teacher writes that being present at the workshop is required for the certificate.
Your company asks if you will come to the Christmas party. Which word means 'participation'?

en: to tell, to align, to line up
situations: Your colleague is out. The caller asks you to pass on a message to her when she returns.
You hang pictures on the wall and adjust them so that they are all in a straight line.
Your mother says: 'When you see Grandpa, please give him my greetings.' Which verb means 'to tell' someone a message?
A rabbit chews a long, orange vegetable that grows underground.
You make soup and peel orange root vegetables with a peeler.
At the market you buy a kilo of long orange roots. Which word means 'carrot'?
After a day at the beach without sun cream, the outer covering of your body is red and hurts.
A doctor checks a strange spot on the outside of your body.
The label of a cream says that it keeps your body's outer covering soft. Which word means 'skin'?

en: in the end, finally, eventually, after all
situations: You tried three restaurants and discussed many ideas. After a long talk you decided on pizza, as the last step.
A friend says: 'Do not be angry with him. He is your brother, after all.'
After waiting an hour at the station, the bus came at last. Which adverb means 'finally'?
Your daughter sings in tune and plays the piano by ear. She has a talent for music.
Your son always hums perfect tunes and keeps the rhythm, even though he never took lessons.
A friend of yours is gifted with sounds and rhythm. Which adjective means 'musical'?
You paid 800 euros at the electronics store and left with a new laptop. The shop gave you a receipt.
A family signs papers to get a house, a big step after years of saving.
On the website you press the button to buy the items in your basket. Which word means 'purchase'?

en: to switch on, to turn on, to power on
situations: It is dark in the room. You press a button on the wall so the lamp comes on.
You sit on the sofa, take the remote and press the red button so the picture appears.
Your laptop is off. You press the power button to start it. Which verb means 'to switch on'?
You open a book and read the first pages that explain what the book is about before the real chapters start.
In your essay, the first paragraph gives the topic and says what you will discuss.
At a presentation, the speaker begins with a few opening words. Which word means 'introduction'?
You watch an episode every evening of a story that has several seasons on a streaming service.
A car maker announces a new model line that will be produced in large numbers.
The football team won five games one after another. Which word means 'series'?

en: to put in, to insert, to use
situations: You get a new battery and place it into the remote control.
At half time, the coach decides to bring the young striker onto the pitch and play him.
You take a missing puzzle piece and put it into the empty space. Which verb means 'to insert'?
You look for the most important street in a small town, not any side street. Which short word part means 'main'?
On the menu, the biggest dish of the meal comes after the starter. The first part of its name means 'main'.
In a film, the person who plays the leading role is called the 'main' actor. Which short word part means 'main'?
Your rent must be paid on the first of the month. Today is the first, so the payment has to be made now.
Your car's technical inspection date has come, so you must go now.
The gym fee has reached its payment date today. Which adjective means 'due'?
You and your friends travel through a jungle with a map, not knowing what will happen next. It is an exciting and risky trip.
A boy reads a book about pirates searching for treasure on a faraway island.
Your friend quit his office job to sail around the world because he wants an exciting experience. Which word means 'adventure'?
You put a DVD into your old computer. Which part of the PC takes it and reads it?
Your computer shows C: and D: as separate places where files are stored.
A technician says the unit inside your computer that stores files is broken. Which word means 'drive'?

en: to put, to plug, to insert, to be (located), to stick
situations: You push the USB stick into the computer port.
You search for your keys everywhere. Then you find them: they were in your jacket pocket all the time.
You push a rose into a vase so that it stands upright. Which verb means 'to put' or 'to stick'?
You spilled water on the table. You grab a soft piece of fabric to wipe it.
It is cold outside. You wrap a piece of fabric around your neck.
You spread a big piece of fabric over the furniture before painting. Which word means 'cloth'?
Your neighbour has different religious views from yours, but you respect them and do not mind.
A teacher accepts that students dress and think differently and never judges them.
A friend lets others live in their own way without complaining. Which adjective means 'tolerant'?
You study abroad. At night you miss your parents, your town and your own bed so much that you feel sad.
A child at summer camp cries because he wants to go back to his family home.
After three months in a foreign country, you feel a strong longing for your home. Which word means 'homesickness'?
A detective checks all the details until he discovers who took the money.
You do not know when the shop opens. You look it up on the internet to get the answer.
Your friend wants to discover the truth about a rumour. Which verb means 'to find out'?
The plumber fixed your leak in ten minutes. You say: 'He really knows his job. He is a real ___.' Which word means 'pro'?
Your colleague solves computer problems quickly and without mistakes. She is certainly no beginner.
For your wedding photos you hire someone who does this as a job, not an amateur. Which word means 'professional'?
Right now you are busy. You tell your friend you will call him later, when your work is over.
First we eat dinner, and after that we will watch a film.
You say: 'Let's talk about it ___.' Which adverb means 'afterwards'?
You add up all the costs of the trip: hotel, flights and food. The result is the full sum. Which short word part means 'total'?
A school reports the overall number of students in all classes together. Which short word part means 'total'?
The teacher gives a final grade made out of all your exam parts together. Which short word part means 'overall'?
A large supermarket gives work and pays wages to two hundred people.
A mother gives the kids a puzzle to keep them busy while she cooks.
The article says the company has 500 people on its payroll. Which verb means 'to employ'?
Every morning loud machines and cranes work where a new house is being made, with workers in helmets.
Your uncle works as a bricklayer, putting up houses.
In the city there is a huge new structure with cranes around it, still unfinished. Which word means 'construction'?
It is raining outside, and you sit on a soft sofa with a blanket, tea and candles. Everything feels warm and relaxed.
A small café has wooden tables, soft light and armchairs, and guests like to stay for hours.
Your friend says her new flat is small but feels warm and homely. Which adjective means 'cosy'?
A footballer gets a salary from a big club and trains every day. Sport is how he earns his living.
A tennis player travels around the world and wins prize money.
Your cousin does not play just for fun at the weekend, he earns a living from sport. Which word means a male 'professional athlete'?
Your phone charger has a long thin line covered in plastic that goes from the plug to the phone.
Your TV picture is gone. Someone pulled the cord behind the cabinet.
Electricians run copper lines through the walls of a new building. Which word means 'cable'?
People gather on the street with signs, shouting that they do not agree with the price increase.
A student openly says to the teacher that the grade is unfair.
Neighbours stand peacefully in front of the town hall to show they are against a new road. Which verb means 'to protest'?
In the morning you open the window to let in fresh something we breathe.
A bicycle tyre is flat. You use a pump to fill it with the invisible gas around us.
In the mountains it is hard to breathe because there is less of it. Which word means 'air'?
You try to open an online account, but the website keeps failing. It is a problem that makes it hard for you.
Learning a new language has many hard parts, like pronouncing strange sounds.
The teacher asks which part of the lesson was the hardest. Which word means 'difficulty'?
Your team just won the final. You jump, shout and cannot stop smiling because you are full of joy.
A child unwraps a present and finds a puppy. She is delighted.
After the concert, the fans clap and talk, full of energy. Which adjective means 'enthusiastic'?

en: to meet, to encounter, to face, to come across
situations: You walk through the park and by chance see your old teacher coming the other way.
On your trip you come across a strange animal on the road.
When travelling, you often meet people with different customs by chance. Which verb means 'to encounter'?
A road sign shows 50. The police use a camera to check how fast cars go.
A sprinter's result is measured by how fast he moves over 100 metres.

A recipe says to mix flour and sugar two to one.

A job ad asks what you can do well, like languages, programming and driving. You list these.
After the accident, the patient lost the power to walk.
A child can remember faces after seeing them only once. Which word means 'ability'?
Your old fridge does not work any more. You take it to a special place to have it properly got rid of.

The hotel price does not include breakfast. You must pay for it as an addition.
You baked this cake specially for your friend's birthday, not for anyone else.
You ask for the sauce in a small bowl on the side, kept apart from the pasta. Which word means 'separately' or 'extra'?
A model has a thin, graceful body and no extra weight.

After frying bacon, a yellowish oily substance stays in the pan.
A nutrition label shows how many grams of this nutrient the chips contain. Too much is unhealthy.
A mechanic puts a thick, oily substance on the bike chain. Which word means 'grease'?

en: to offer, to provide, to bid
situations: At an auction you raise your hand and say you will pay 500 euros for the painting.
A hotel says its rooms give guests a view of the sea, a pool and free breakfast.
The company wants to give you a new job with better pay. Which verb means 'to offer'?
On a hot day you move under a tree where the sun does not reach, and it feels cooler.
In the evening your dark outline stretches long across the road behind you as the sun goes down.
A child makes funny animal shapes on the wall with her hands in front of a lamp. Which word means 'shadow'?
Your friend did not come to the party. You ask why, because you want to hear the cause.
A swimmer dives down and touches the lowest part of the lake.
The teacher says: 'You have no ___ to be nervous.' Which word means 'reason'?
You tried for an hour to open the stuck door, but nothing worked and you gave up.
He waited at the station all night, but she never came. His effort brought no result.
All the searching for the lost key was pointless. Which adjective means 'futile'?

en: to address, to bring sth up
situations: At the party you see an interesting person and decide to go over and start talking to her.
You want to bring up a problem with your boss at the meeting.
A stranger in the street walks up and speaks to you to ask for directions. Which verb means 'to address' someone?
After a hard year at work, you spend two weeks at the beach, doing nothing and relaxing.
After the flu, the doctor says you need time to get better and regain strength.
A sign at the spa says it is a place for rest and relaxation. Which word means 'recovery'?
The school asks: which kind of sport do you like, football, swimming, tennis or basketball?
At the Olympics there are many different disciplines such as running, boxing and rowing.
A form for the club asks you to tick which sport you want to do. Which word means 'type of sport'?
Two bakeries on the same street try to win the same customers. Each watches what the other does.

In a race, many other runners are trying to win against you. Which word means 'competition'?
You download a new program and run the setup so it works on your laptop.
A technician fits a new washing machine in your kitchen and connects it to the water.

A man stands at the side of the football pitch, shouting instructions to the team and choosing the players.

You go to the same bakery almost every morning, many times a week.

Forty people join the language course. A man who sits in the room and takes part is one of them.

The organiser of a conference counts everyone who registered. Which word means a male 'participant'?

en: to copy, to plagiarize, to transcribe, to write off, to depreciate
situations: During the exam, a student looks at his neighbour's paper and copies the answers. The teacher is angry.
You copy the text from the board into your notebook by hand.
The company decides the old machine has lost its value and records the loss in its accounts. Which verb means 'to write off'?

Smoking increases the possibility of getting sick. Which word means 'risk'?

A psychologist talks with you every week to help you with your fears.
The doctor plans a course of medical treatment for your illness over several weeks. Which word means 'therapy'?
Your daughter wins first prize in the school competition. You watch her on stage with a big smile and feel very happy about her success.

A job ad says you must have a university degree before you can apply. That is the first thing needed.

The doctor says you sit too much and should do more physical activity, like walking every day.
A dancer's arms and legs flow in beautiful graceful steps across the stage.
A car stands still, and then it starts to roll forward. Which word means 'motion'?
After playing in the garden in the rain, the kids' shoes are covered in wet earth and mess.
The floor in the kitchen is really filthy, and you must clean it.

en: to run, to race, to sprint
situations: The bus is leaving in one minute. You move as fast as you can on your legs to catch it.
A dog chases a ball across the park at full speed.

en: course instructor, course leader, course director
situations: At the evening school a man stands in front of the class, teaches the course and makes the schedule.

After the operation, the patient tells the nurses how happy he is for all their care.

en: to be boring, to bore, to be bored

Bottles, toys and bags are often made of this light material that factories produce from oil.

A child holds her father's hand and knows he will never let go.

The farmer lives on his land with cows, chickens and a barn.
The castle has a big open square surrounded by walls. Which word means 'courtyard'?
Guests arrive at your house. You stand at the door, smile and say hello to each of them.
The mayor opens the event and says a few friendly words to the visitors.
The teacher says good morning to the class as they enter. Which verb means 'to greet'?
In art class, you make a picture with a pencil on paper.
The architect shows a rough picture of the building before the final plans.
A child gives her mother a picture she made with crayons. Which word means 'drawing'?
You did not understand the teacher. You ask her to say it one more time.
The first try failed, so you try one more time.
The song is so good that you listen to it again. Which adverb means 'once more'?
A man started his own company with five employees and runs it himself.
A man has an idea for a business, takes the risk and creates jobs for others.
The man who owns the firm pays wages to the workers. Which word means a male 'entrepreneur'?
You have enough food in the fridge for the whole weekend, so there is no need to shop.
The teacher says the answers are just enough to pass, with a grade of 4.
Is the light in this room enough to read by? Which adjective means 'sufficient'?
At a German restaurant, the roast comes with a round ball made from potato dough, served with gravy.
Grandma boils round balls of potato dough in water.
Round potato balls boiled in water are a typical side dish. Which word means 'dumpling'?
A truck carries goods from the harbour to the warehouse.
The ambulance brings the injured man to the hospital.
The company moves heavy machines by ship. Which verb means 'to transport'?
You drive from one country to another and officers check passports at the line between them.
A fence marks where your garden ends and your neighbour's begins.
Tourists cross the line between two countries. Which word means 'border'?
A man pays 600 euros every month to live in a flat that he does not own.
The landlord sends a letter to the man who lives in the flat about the rent increase.
A man signs a contract to live in a flat and pays rent. Which word means a male 'tenant'?

en: to be certain, to be fixed, to be clear, to be determined, to be established
situations: The date of the wedding is already decided: 12 June. Nothing will change.
The boss says it is now clear that the meeting takes place on Monday.
Everything is already settled and cannot be changed. Which verb means 'to be fixed'?
At first, the plan was to travel by train, but we changed it. How do you describe the plan from the start?
The old church still has its first form, and nothing has been changed.
The forest is untouched by people, wild and natural. Which adjective means 'original' or 'unspoiled'?
You have a runny nose, a cough and a sore throat, and you stay in bed for three days.
In winter, many people sneeze and feel weak because of a mild illness.
You tell your boss you cannot come in because you have caught a mild illness with sneezing. Which word means 'a cold'?
At the restaurant, before the main dish, you order a small soup.
The waiter asks what you would like to eat first, before the big dish.
On the menu: soup or salad, served before the main course. Which word means 'starter'?
You greet a stranger with a friendly face and a small curve of your lips, without laughing.
When the photographer asks for happy faces, the children show them.
A baby looks at her mother and shows a small happy expression. Which verb means 'to smile'?
A woman on the street asks you five questions about your shopping habits for a study.
The newspaper asked 1,000 people who their favourite singer is.
The school asks all students in a form about the canteen. Which word means 'survey'?
You arrive at the station just as your train leaves. What terrible luck!
It rained on the only day of your holiday when you wanted to go to the beach.
You have a flat tyre on the way to an important meeting. Which word means 'bad luck'?
You did not plan it. You met your teacher at the supermarket.
The glass fell down without anyone wanting it to.
You happened to find the key under the sofa. Which adjective means 'by chance'?
While showering, you suddenly think of a clever solution for your project.
A child comes up with a funny plan to hide the vegetables.
In a brainstorm the team shares many quick thoughts. Which word means 'idea'?
You touch a hot pan and notice the heat on your fingers.
In the room you notice that something is wrong. You can feel it.
Your skin senses the wind on your face. Which verb means 'to feel'?
A mother works only four hours a day, mornings only.
A job ad says: 'We need someone for the morning only, not the full day.'
You do not work full-time but for half of the working day. Which adverb means 'part-time'?
An actor plays a character in the new film.
In the shop, you buy a cylinder of toilet paper.
In a project every member has a task and a part to play. Which word means 'role'?
In the morning you squeeze a white paste onto your brush.
The dentist recommends a paste with fluoride for cleaning your teeth.
At the pharmacy you buy a tube for brushing your teeth. Which word means 'toothpaste'?

en: to avoid, to bypass, to circumvent, to handle, to deal with
situations: The road ahead is closed, so you take a different route around it.
A firm finds a trick to avoid paying taxes.
A child learns how to deal with a sharp knife safely. Which verb means 'to handle'?
A man who lives in Germany and has a German passport belongs to the country with rights and duties.
The mayor invites the people of the city to a meeting. Every man who belongs to the state is welcome.
A man has the nationality of a country. Which word means a male 'citizen'?
In a good marriage, the husband and wife have the same rights and decide things together.
At the company, women and men have the same chances and equal rights.
Everyone should have the same standing before the law. Which adjective means 'with equal rights'?
At the hotel the receptionist asks for your name, date of birth and address.
On the application form, there is a section for your name, address and birthday.
The police officer asks to see your ID to check your name and address. Which word means 'personal details'?
In front of the garage, there is a short paved road where the car goes in.
A sign at the front says 'Do not block' because it is the way into the courtyard for cars.
The sign at the car park says 'Entrance for vehicles'. Which word means 'driveway' or 'entry'?

en: to type, to tap, to tip
situations: You write a message on the keyboard with your fingers.
You touch the screen of the phone lightly with a finger.
You guess the result of the football match, for example 2:1, in a betting game. Which verb means 'to tip'?
He firmly believes in his opinion and nobody can change his mind.
In an interview, a man says that he lives as a vegetarian because of his strong belief.
After a long talk, you managed to make him agree with you. Which word means 'conviction'?
The bakery is only two minutes away from your flat.
The airport is close to the city centre.
Your friend lives not far from you. Which adjective means 'near'?
Before you buy a car, you calculate petrol, insurance and repairs.
The bill for the repair shows the amount you have to pay for the work.
The bank asks about your monthly expenses. Which word means 'costs'?
The plane touches the runway and rolls to a stop.
The pilot says that we will be on the ground in ten minutes.
A bird comes down from the sky and sits on a branch. Which verb means 'to land'?
In summer, many German families go to the coast in the north and see the tides and islands like Sylt.
It is the sea to the north of Germany, between Britain and Denmark and Norway.
On the map of Europe you see the sea between Britain and Scandinavia. Which word is its name, 'the North Sea'?
In your living room there is a piece of furniture along the wall with many levels for books.
At the supermarket the goods stand on long boards in rows.
You put your books on a board attached to the wall. Which word means 'shelf'?

en: together, with each other, to each other
situations: The two brothers always speak with one another in a friendly way.
The family sits at the table and talks, each one with the others.
In a good team, people help one another. Which adverb means 'with each other'?

en: to cheat, to defraud, to betray, to trick, to deceive
situations: A shopkeeper gives you less change than he should, and he does it on purpose.
He tells his wife he works late but secretly meets another woman. He is not faithful to her.
A fake website takes people's money and never sends anything. Which verb means 'to cheat' or 'to defraud'?
During your three-week visit to Germany you live in Hamburg.
Your train has a 20-minute stop in the station before it goes on.
Your visa lets you remain in the country for 90 days. Which word means 'stay'?
There is just one seat left in the whole bus, and nobody else has one.
You are the one child at the party. There is not another.
Only one thing matters to you, nothing else. Which adjective means 'only' or 'sole'?
Tomorrow your class writes a test on maths.
After school you sit at your desk and do the exercises the teacher gave you to finish at home.
Your mother asks: 'Have you done your tasks for school?' Which word means 'homework'?
A man walks on the pavement and waits for the green light to cross the street.
At the zebra crossing, a man on foot crosses and the cars have to stop.
A road sign shows a figure of a person walking. Which word means a male 'pedestrian'?

en: to create, to build, to draw up, to produce
situations: You open a program and make a list of all the guests for the party.
An engineer produces a plan for a new bridge.
The accountant prepares the annual report. Which verb means 'to draw up' or 'to create'?
The police find fingerprints and want to know who did the robbery. They look for the man responsible.
The court finds the man who committed the crime.
The police arrest the man who carried out the theft. Which word means a male 'culprit'?
You dreamed that you could fly, but when you wake up, you remember the real world.
In the film everything is perfect, but life as it truly is, is not.
A friend says your plan is nice in theory, but what happens in real life is different. Which word means 'reality'?
After five years in Germany, you speak German without stopping to look for words.
In the kitchen, the tap gives hot and cold water that moves continuously.
A job ad asks for English that is smooth and without mistakes. Which adjective means 'fluent'?
Twin sisters look alike, but their mother can tell which is which.
A wine expert can tell different grapes by their flavour.
You learn to see the difference between two similar words. Which verb means 'to distinguish'?
While the parents work, a person looks after the children at the day-care centre.
A nurse takes care of an old woman at home.
A university offers a programme where someone guides you through your thesis. Which word means 'support' or 'care'?
Price is one of several things that influence your decision to buy a car.
In maths, two numbers multiplied together give a result. Each of those numbers is one of these.
The weather was an important element in the result of the race. Which word means 'factor'?
Cars drive on the part of the street between the pavements.
A sign says that cyclists should use the part of the street meant for vehicles.
Children should never play on the part of the road where cars go. Which word means 'roadway'?

en: to amuse oneself, to enjoy oneself, to have a good time, to have fun
situations: At the fair the kids go on rides and eat sweets and have a great time.
On Saturday night, the students go dancing and enjoy themselves.
Your friend says he wants to amuse himself at the party. Which verb means 'to enjoy oneself'?
This room is for staff only, no one else.
She eats only vegetables, nothing else.
The shop sells nothing but shoes. Which word means 'exclusively'?
The teacher says an essay needs a beginning, a middle and an end. She talks about how the whole text is organised.
You draw boxes to plan which paragraph comes where in your report.
In the writing course you learn how paragraphs link into one piece. Which word means 'text structure'?
You are parking your car and need to move it back into the space, looking over your shoulder.
A child walks with his face forward but takes steps toward his back.
You say the alphabet starting with Z and ending with A. Which adverb means 'backwards'?
She started as a trainee and in ten years became the director of the company. Her professional path went up quickly.
He puts work first because he wants to climb the ladder in his profession.
At school the counsellor asks what job path you want. Which word means 'career'?

en: to fit in, to insert, to paste
situations: You copy a sentence from one document and put it into another.
You add a new word to the middle of a sentence you have written.
The last puzzle piece must be put into its place. Which verb means 'to insert'?
You look up an unknown word in the dictionary to find out what it stands for.
The teacher says the discovery is very important for science.
A road sign shows a red circle. What does it express? Which word means 'meaning'?
A researcher studies how all the people living together in a country behave and are organised.
You sit alone at dinner and wish for somebody to be there with you.
The newspaper discusses problems of the whole community of people in a nation. Which word means 'society'?
The vase is broken, and your little brother says it was your fault.
Nobody wants to take the blame for the accident.
You forgot to lock the door, so it is your fault that the thief came in. Which word describes someone who is 'to blame'?
You promised your child a trip to the zoo but cancel it, and he feels let down.
The film had a lot of hype but was boring. It did not meet your hopes.
The coach is upset because the players did not meet his hopes. Which verb means 'to disappoint'?
A black and white bird walks upright on the ice in Antarctica and cannot fly.
At the zoo, a bird that looks like it wears a tuxedo waddles and swims.
Which bird lives in the cold south, swims well, cannot fly and has a white belly? Which word means 'penguin'?
An antique expert says the vase is worth 5,000 euros.
The price tag says one number, but what the thing is really worth to you is more.
The test result shows a number for your blood sugar. Which word means 'value'?
In the morning at the baker's, you buy a small round bread with a crispy crust to eat with butter and cheese.
For breakfast you cut open a small round bread and put ham in it.
In Bavaria you ask for a small round bread at the bakery. Which word means 'bread roll'?
You turn your eyes toward the window to see the snow.
In the evening you sit on the sofa and view a film on TV.
Your mother calls you to come and see something. Which verb means 'to look'?
Your friend has packed his bags and put on his shoes. He says he can go now.
The student is willing to help with the project and says he is prepared.
Dinner is cooked and the table is set. Which adjective means 'ready'?
You lost your wallet and with it all your money and cards.
The company made less money than it spent, so it ended the year with negative numbers.
The family is sad after the death of the grandfather and feels a big emptiness. Which word means 'loss'?
A man in the hospital changes the patient's bandage and checks his temperature.
In a care home for old people, a man helps the residents wash and eat.
A man works with the sick on the ward. Which word means a 'male nurse'?

en: to use, to utilize, to utilise, to take advantage
situations: You have a free hour, so you make good use of it to study.
It is a sunny day, so you take advantage of it for a picnic.
Many people employ the bike lanes every day. Which verb means 'to use'?
A man robs banks and the police look for him. He breaks the law seriously.
In the film, the detective chases a man who has committed serious crimes.
The prison holds men who broke the law. Which word means 'criminal'?
The teacher is not pleased with how the students act in class, too loud and rude.
A zoo researcher watches how the monkeys act in groups.
A child shows good manners at the table. Which word means 'behaviour'?
You are in the kitchen and your friend asks where your sister is. You say she was here a moment ago.
You have only now finished the report. You finished it moments ago.
Your phone rang a second ago. Which adverb means 'just now'?
In the desert, the temperature goes far beyond the normal.
She climbs mountains in the most dangerous conditions, a sport with great risks.
The cold in Siberia in winter is beyond ordinary. Which adjective means 'extreme'?
In the concert hall, about eighty musicians with violins, flutes and drums play together under a conductor.
A conductor stands in front of a group of musicians playing classical music.
The school has a big group of students playing violins, flutes and trumpets together. Which word means 'orchestra'?

en: to leave, to abandon, to forsake, to desert
situations: At six you walk out of the house and close the door behind you.
A father walks away from his family and leaves them alone.
The passengers go out of the train at the last stop. Which verb means 'to leave'?

You read the 'rooms for rent' notes in the newspaper.
A small notice in the paper offers a used sofa for sale. Which word means 'advertisement'?
