At the market, apples are sold in wooden containers.
A strong container made of wood or plastic is used for transport. Which word means 'crate'?

en: to take, to take over, to take on, to assume
situations: Your boss leaves the company, and you now take charge of his tasks.
At the restaurant, a friend says: 'I will pay the bill.' He takes it over.
You agree to look after the project from now on. Which verb means 'to take over'?
You have not cleaned the shelf for months and a grey layer covers it.
When the car drives on the dry road, a cloud of fine dry earth rises.
Your finger writes in the fine grey powder on the table. Which word means 'dust'?
The ceiling in the cellar is so close to your head that you must bend.
The price of the ticket is small, far less than you expected.
The bridge is not high, and the fence is only waist-high. Which adjective means 'low'?
In a boxing match, there are twelve parts of three minutes each.
The runner completes one lap of the track.
At the pub, you buy drinks for everyone in the group because it is your turn. Which word means 'round'?
The doctor tells you to move your arm slowly up and down.
The wind makes the leaves shift.
You cannot lift the heavy sofa. You cannot shift it from its place. Which verb means 'to move' something?
In winter in the cold wind, the soft skin around your mouth gets dry and cracked.
You apply colour on the edges of your mouth before going out.
You press the edges of your mouth together to stay quiet. Which word means 'lip'?
The supermarket sells bread, milk, rice and eggs, things people eat to live.
After the flood, aid workers give out things to eat to the villagers.
In a store, the shelves contain things we can eat. Which word means 'food'?
A boy sticks out his tongue at the teacher and answers back rudely.
A child says to an adult: 'You are old!' with a smirk, showing no respect but not meaning harm.
Your neighbour's son talks to you in a bold, disrespectful way. Which adjective means 'cheeky'?
The weightlifter needs great physical power to raise the heavy bar.
The wind has such force that it blows the roof off.
After a good night's sleep you feel full of energy. Which word means 'strength'?

en: to mix up, to mistake, to confuse
situations: You take someone else's umbrella because it looks just like yours.
You think that Maria is Anna. They look alike, so you call her by the wrong name.
The pharmacist gave you the wrong medicine by confusing two boxes. Which verb means 'to mix up'?
A girl has no brothers or sisters and grows up alone with her parents.
In your class, one boy says he has never shared a room with a sibling.
Your friend is the only child in the family. Which word means 'only child'?
Someone says: 'Have a nice weekend!' and you answer: 'The same to you!'
The waiter says: 'Enjoy your meal!' and you politely wish him the same.
A friend wishes you luck, and you want to say it back. Which adverb means 'likewise'?
The road is closed because of construction, and signs send you along a different route.
A yellow sign shows an arrow telling drivers to go another way around.
The bridge is closed, so the traffic takes a longer route. Which word means 'detour'?

en: to bring up, to educate, to raise, to teach
situations: Parents teach their children good manners, how to behave and to be honest, for many years.
A single mother is raising two kids on her own.
A grandmother helped to look after and form the grandchildren as they grew up. Which verb means 'to bring up'?
Astronauts look out of the spaceship window at the blue planet where we live.
In the garden, you dig in the dark brown soil and plant seeds.
A farmer picks up a handful of soil and lets it fall through his fingers. Which word means 'earth' or 'soil'?
Before the exam, you study eight hours a day, very hard and focused.
The colours in the painting are very strong and bright.
The patients in this ward get very thorough care. Which adjective describes this kind of 'intensive' care?

en: instructions for use, directions for use, operating instructions, user manual
situations: You buy a new coffee machine and unfold a paper leaflet that explains how to operate it.
The medicine box includes a leaflet that explains how to take the tablets.
You cannot work out how to start the washing machine, so you search for the booklet that explains it. Which word means 'user manual'?
The tax office asks how much money you earn a year from all sources.
A family with a low monthly sum of money coming in gets help from the state.
A form asks for your yearly earnings from work. Which word means 'income'?
In the football game, the player strikes the ball with his foot.
You move one foot forward and put it on the first stair.
You accidentally put your foot on someone's toes in the bus. Which verb means 'to step' on something?
On Sunday, mum cooks a big piece of meat in the oven with gravy.
Your grandmother serves a big piece of pork cooked in the oven with potatoes.
A butcher sells a large piece of beef for the oven. Which word means 'roast'?
You can hardly read the old letter because the style of the letters is so strange.
In the document program, you choose the style of letters and the size for the text.
Archaeologists found stone tablets covered with signs of an ancient language, an early writing system. Which word means 'script'?
In a dry summer, water becomes hard to get. There is not enough of it.
He passed the exam by a tiny margin, just barely.
The trousers are very tight around the waist. Which adjective means 'tight'?

en: to separate, to disconnect, to isolate
situations: You put plastic, paper and glass in different bins for waste.
You pull the plug out of the socket to cut the connection to the power.
A wall divides the room into two parts. Which verb means 'to separate'?
The football player falls and has a broken leg. He must miss the next games.
The police report that a driver broke traffic rules, a breach of the law.
The doctor looks at the damage to your ankle after you fell. Which word means 'injury'?
You drive to the place where the land ends and the sea begins and walk along the beach.
A lighthouse stands where the land meets the sea.
A ship sails near the edge of the land. Which word means 'coast'?

en: to participate, to take part, to contribute
situations: Everyone in the class joins the discussion and gives an opinion.
A company puts some money into the project, too.
You sign up for the charity run and take part. Which verb means 'to participate'?
You have dry, red skin on your elbow, and the doctor gives you a creamy medicine to rub on it.
After a bee sting, you put a soothing cream on the red spot.
The pharmacy sells a thick medical cream in a tube. Which word means 'ointment'?
The shop is open Monday to Friday but closed on Sunday. What does the sign say about those days?
On days when people work, the train is full. On Sundays, it is empty.
The restaurant opens at 7 am from Monday to Friday, but later at the weekend. Which adverb means 'on weekdays'?
She wears a nice dress and her face is lovely to look at.
The village has charming little houses with flowers.
A friend shows you a photo of a cute girl. Which adjective means 'pretty'?
From the top floor window you look at the mountains and the lake.
After finishing your studies, your chances of getting a good job are high.
The hotel room has a lovely sight of the sea. Which word means 'view'?
In the first grade, children learn the letters from A to Z in order.
You sing a song with all the letters of a language in order.
Words in a dictionary are arranged by the order of letters. Which word means 'alphabet'?
In the shoe shop you look at ten pairs and pick the black ones.
In the bakery, you take your time deciding which cake to buy.
The teacher asks each student to select a topic. Which verb means 'to choose'?
A company gives money to young artists to help them develop their talent.
The state helps the student with a grant to pay for his studies.
Employers support the training of workers. Which word means 'support' or 'sponsorship'?
You lost your passport abroad and go to the official building of your country in that capital to get help.
The speech carries an important point to the people. What is its main point?
A diplomat works at the official representation of a country in a foreign capital. Which word means 'embassy'?
The doctor says the result is favourable and the news is good.
Your attitude is optimistic. You always see the good side.
The teacher gives feedback with praise. Which adjective means 'positive'?
You write a note and put it on the table before you go out so that your family reads it.
The old man died and gave his house to his children as an inheritance.
The guest wrote a message in the hotel's book before going. Which verb means 'to leave' something behind?
In the bathroom, you look at your face on a glass surface on the wall.
In the car, you check the traffic behind you using a small glass on the side.
Snow White's stepmother asked a magic one on the wall. Which word means 'mirror'?
A young woman studies for six years at university to become a doctor.
The doctor gives you tablets from the pharmacy.
The pharmacy sells drugs for illness. Which word means 'medicine'?
In a German restaurant, you order a thin piece of meat covered with breadcrumbs and fried, with potatoes.
Mum flattens a thin slice of pork or veal, covers it with crumbs and fries it.
A famous Viennese dish is a breaded fried cutlet. Which word means 'schnitzel'?
During summer, you stay at your grandparents' village for two weeks, passing the time.
You like to pass your evenings reading at home.
How do you pass your weekends? Which verb means 'to spend' time?

en: punctual, in time, in good time, on time, timely
situations: You arrive at the station five minutes before the train leaves. You did not miss it.
The ambulance came early enough to save the patient.
You hand in your homework before the deadline. Which adjective means 'in time'?
It is cold, so you put something soft on your foot before your shoes.
After washing, one of the pair is missing and you cannot find the other.
Your grandmother knits a woollen piece for your foot as a Christmas present. Which word means 'sock'?
The article is divided into three parts, and you read the second part.
A road is under construction in one stretch between two exits.
In your essay, the teacher marks one part under a separate heading. Which word means 'section'?

en: to enter, to join, to happen, to occur
situations: You knock on the door, open it and walk into the office.
You decide to become a member of the club. You go in as a member.
The doctor says: 'If a fever sets in, call me.' Which verb means 'to occur' or 'to join'?
You stand at the bottom of the stairs and say: 'Come ___ here!' Which small word means 'up'?
A hill is in front of you and your friend says: 'Let's go ___!' Which adverb means 'up'?
The cat is in the garden and the child says: 'Climb ___ the tree.' Which word means 'up' as a direction?
At the doctor's, the nurse prepares a needle to put medicine in your arm.
Before travelling, you get a vaccination in your upper arm.
It is a tool with a plunger and a needle. Which word means 'syringe'?
On your breakfast bread you spread a sweet fruit preserve made from strawberries.
Grandma cooks fruit with sugar and fills glass jars.
In the supermarket you pick a jar of sweet fruit spread. Which word means 'jam'?
Your boss lets you start work at eight or at ten, depending on what suits you.
A rubber band can be bent a lot and does not break.
You are ready to change plans quickly if needed. Which adjective means 'flexible'?

en: to bet, to wager, to gamble
situations: You say to your friend: 'I will give you 10 euros if our team does not win.'
At the horse races, people put money on a horse.
You are sure it will rain tomorrow and offer to risk money on it. Which verb means 'to bet'?
Before moving to Germany, you attend a language course every day for six hours for one month.
A summer school offers a very fast and demanding course of four weeks, every day.
You choose a short, hard, full-time course to learn quickly. Which word means 'intensive course'?
On a big grass course with small holes, a player hits a little white ball with a club.
A famous sport is played outdoors on large green areas, and players carry many clubs in a bag.
Which sport uses clubs, a small ball and eighteen holes?
You open the toolbox and take out a hammer, a screwdriver and pliers.
A mechanic needs the right instrument to loosen the screw.
A hammer is something you use to do work with your hands. Which word means 'tool'?

en: to reach, to be enough, to last, to suffice, to pass
situations: You have 10 euros. The ticket costs 8. Is that enough?
The food in the fridge will last until Sunday.
At the table, you ask someone to hand you the salt. Which verb means 'to pass'?
The village lies on a small rise in the landscape, lower than a mountain.
The children roll down a small grassy rise in the park.
Between the flat fields, a small elevated area rises. Which word means 'hill'?
The picture on the wall is not hanging straight. One corner is lower than the other.
The tower of the old church is leaning to one side.
Your line on the paper goes up and down, not straight. Which adjective means 'crooked'?
A man looks at your old car and says he wants to pay for it.
In an online shop, a man puts the product in his cart and pays.
The seller waits for a man who will pay for the flat. Which word means a male 'buyer'?

en: to receive, to get, to obtain, to preserve, to maintain
situations: A letter arrives in your mailbox and you take it.
The old building is still in good condition because the city keeps it from falling apart.
You get a prize for your results. Which verb means 'to receive'?
On the piano, you press a white or black bar to make a sound.
On your computer keyboard, you press the one marked 'Enter'.
The calculator has a small pad for each number. Which word means 'key' or 'button'?
Fishermen throw a mesh of strings into the sea to catch fish.
Your phone shows no connection to the system of mobile signals.
A spider builds a pattern of threads between two branches to catch insects. Which word means 'web' or 'net'?

en: in the middle, in the center, amidst, in the midst
situations: The tree stands exactly halfway between the two ends of the field, neither near one side nor the other.

A boy dreams of getting one on his 18th birthday.

en: to put on, to fasten (seat belt), to buckle up
situations: You get in the car and pull the belt over your shoulder until it clicks.
The flight attendant says to put on your belt for landing.
A child sits in the back and the mother checks that the belt is on.
The train drivers stop work for a day to demand more pay.
Workers do not go to work to protest and the trains do not run.
The teachers refuse to work today.
The flat has a good price, two rooms and is near your work. It is perfect.
For a picnic, the weather is perfect.
He is the perfect candidate.
You add all the test scores and divide: a student has 2.5 as his middle result.
What is the middle result of 4, 6 and 8?
The statistics say that a person eats 80 kilos of meat per year in the middle of all people.
Stealing is forbidden by the rules of the country, written by parliament.
A policeman explains that the rule of the country says you cannot drive after drinking.
The new rule was passed after a long debate.

en: to pay attention, to note, to observe
situations: The sign says: 'Please note the opening hours.'
A driver must pay attention to the traffic rules.
Please follow the instructions on the box.
You put your head on a soft thing in your bed.
On the sofa, there are small soft squares for decoration.
A soft thing on a chair helps you sit comfortably.
After work, a warm bath makes you calm and loose.
A walk in the quiet forest gives you rest.
Soft music helps you calm down.

en: for nothing, in vain, for free, free (of charge)
situations: The museum gives free entry to students. They do not pay anything.
You studied all night, but you did not pass. It was without success.
The shop gives you a sample for nothing.
A yellow shiny metal is used for rings.
The winner at the Olympics receives a medal of this precious metal.
Pirates look for treasure: coins made of this.

en: to report, to signal, to notify, to announce, to inform
situations: Someone hits your car, so you call the police to tell them.
A pupil raises his hand to tell the teacher he knows the answer.
You go to the town hall to register your new address.
Strong wind breaks tree branches and shakes the windows.
The weather service warns of heavy wind and rain tonight.
The ship fights big waves and wind.
At university, a man gives the main lectures and does research.
A student says: 'I will write my thesis with the man who has the highest teaching rank.'
Albert Einstein was one.
You carry a heavy backpack on one part of your body between neck and arm.
A friend taps you on this body part to get your attention.
When you do not know the answer, you raise both of them.

en: to set, to fix, to determine, to settle, to collect
situations: The teacher decides on a date for the test: 'We will fix it for Monday.'
The council sets the price for parking.
The two sides agree and settle the amount.
A song is known in every country of the world.
The company sells phones on all continents.
The disease spread across the whole planet.
A woman saved three children from a fire. Everybody calls her this.
In a film, the main woman fights the bad guys and saves the town.
A girl says her mother is her biggest idol because she is so brave.
A teacher tells you step by step why your answer is wrong.
A witness gives a written account to the police.
You hand in a tax form where you state your income.
A child firmly says no to eating vegetables and closes his mouth.
The customer says he will not pay the bill.
A worker says he will not do the task.
A small cardboard container holds chocolates.
A small paper container holds matches.
A cardboard container with a lid holds shoes.
After a marathon, the runner cannot stand up. He has no energy left.
A mother with a newborn has not slept for days. She is totally tired.
You worked 14 hours without breaks and you are worn out.
A newspaper report gives a one-sided description of what happened.
A witness's version of the events differs from another.
In your presentation you show in pictures how the machine works.
The alarm rings at 6:00 and you open your eyes.
A baby opens his eyes and cries in the middle of the night.
After a long operation, the patient returns to consciousness.
On the motorway, you leave the road at number 12.
The sign at the car park shows the way out for cars.
The navigation says: 'Take the next one.'
You want to sell your bike and put a short text in the newspaper.
On the last page of the magazine, short texts offer rooms for rent.
A company pays for a small text to promote its product.
Last time you lost, but on this occasion you win.
You were late yesterday. Please do not be late on this occasion.
'I forgave you once, but now I am serious.' Which adverb means 'on this occasion'?
Back from Paris, you bring your mother a small Eiffel tower.
Tourists buy small objects with the city's name to remember the trip.
A shop near the cathedral sells postcards, mugs and magnets.

en: to bite, to sting, to clash
situations: A dog catches your trouser leg with its teeth.
You eat an apple and use your teeth.
A mosquito attacks you at night.
The old watch costs 500 euros. It is valuable and good value for the price.
'Is this book worth reading?'
The ring is valued at 1000 euros.
It is not an opinion. It is a proven truth: the earth goes around the sun.
A reporter checks his facts before writing.
'Is it true or just a rumour?' 'It is reality.'
At the town hall, officials handle papers, permits and registrations.
A manager is responsible for running the company's internal affairs.
The university's office handles students' files and fees.
You wear a helmet so your head does not get hurt.
Parents hold their child close when a dog barks.
Sun cream keeps your skin from burning.
He always tells funny jokes and makes everyone laugh. He has a sense of fun.
British people are said to have a dry sense of funny things.
You laugh at a hard situation instead of crying.
Journalists and newspapers as a group: reporters from them were at the event.
A machine squeezes oranges to make juice.
A big machine pushes metal sheets into shape.
You poke the potatoes with a fork. They are soft and ready to eat.
The steak is no longer raw. It is finished cooking.
The rice has boiled for 15 minutes and it is ready now.
You open a metal container of tomatoes with a can opener.
A small round metal box with a lid holds sweets.
A drink comes in a metal cylinder from the supermarket.
You decide not to give back the gift. You keep it.
'You can keep the change.'
A student remembers the vocabulary he learned.
A car has four of them. They are round.
A child learns to ride one with two wheels and pedals.
The tyre goes flat and the round part must be changed.
A jacket is made from the skin of cows. It is tough and shiny.
A shoe shop sells boots made from animal skin.
The covering of the sofa is made of soft animal skin.

en: to stop, to hold up, to delay
situations: A policeman steps in front of the thief to make him stop.
A traffic accident holds up the cars, and I am late.
'Sorry, I do not want to keep you from your work.'
You go to the gym every Monday, Wednesday and Friday without missing.
A bus comes every ten minutes.
A dentist says you should check your teeth twice a year, at fixed times.
A married couple decides to end the marriage officially at court.
After 20 years, the husband and wife go separate ways.
Their children live with Mum after their parents' marriage ended.

en: a short while ago, a moment ago, earlier
situations: 'Where is Anna?' 'She was here a moment ago.'
You say you saw him a short time ago on the street.
'The phone rang earlier, but I did not answer.'
It is a period of ten years, like the 1990s.
Over the past ten years, prices have doubled.
'It happened many of these ago' means 30 or 40 years ago.
You hold a ball in your hand and send it through the air to your friend.
A boy sends a stone into the river.
You send the rubbish into the bin from a distance.
Nike and Adidas are famous names of products.
You put a small paper on the envelope before posting it.
'Which name of toothpaste do you buy?'
Your grandmother cannot live alone anymore. She moves to a place where nurses care for old people.
A school class visits and sings for the elderly in their building.
Many old people live together in a building with nurses.
A drawing has many colours, not black and white.
The children's book has bright pictures.
The painter's pictures were bright and had many shades.
A friend is in hospital. You write on the card: 'Get well soon.'
The doctor says: 'There is improvement after the treatment. He is getting well again.'
On a get-well card, you write: 'I wish you a quick recovery.'

en: to decide, to determine, to rule
situations: You stand in front of two jackets in a shop for ten minutes. At last you choose the blue one and walk to the cash desk.
Two companies offer you a job. After thinking all week, you tell both of them which one you pick.
You and your friends cannot agree where to eat tonight. Someone must make the final choice. Which verb means 'to decide'?
A huge flood destroys a whole town, and thousands of people lose their homes. What kind of event is this?
You forgot your passport, missed your flight and lost your hotel booking, all on the same day. You say it was a total ... day. Which noun fits?
On the news you see pictures of a terrible earthquake. Which word means 'disaster'?
You go to a shop to buy cotton or wool by the metre, because you want to sew a dress yourself.
A tailor shows you rolls in different colours and patterns for your new suit and lets you touch each one.
In science class you learn that water, salt and sugar are different kinds of matter. Which word means 'substance'?
You need your train ticket on paper. You click a button on your computer and the page comes out of the machine.
At the office your boss asks you to put the email from your screen onto paper for the meeting.
You finish your homework on the laptop and send it to the printer so you can bring a paper copy to school. What do you do with the file?
On your first day at university, a first lecture gives a short overview of the whole course before the real lessons begin.
A new employee gets a short talk about the company and its rules before starting the real work.
The first pages of a book explain what the book is about and why the writer wrote it. Which word means 'introduction'?
You hear a noise in the empty house at night, and you cannot explain where it comes from. It feels not normal at all.
Your neighbour wears a thick winter coat in the summer heat and talks to himself. His behaviour is not what people expect.
A friend suddenly stops talking to you for no reason. You say: this is really ... Which adjective means 'odd'?
You wrote a novel and send your manuscript to the company that prints and sells books.
On the first page of a book you see the name and address of the company that brought it out.
You work in an office where editors prepare new books and magazines for sale. What kind of company is it? Which word means 'publisher'?
A road sign shows the number 50 in a red circle. The police may fine you if you drive faster than that.
On the motorway near the town, a sign shows 100 because of noise. It tells drivers the fastest speed they may drive.
Your driving teacher says you must always watch for signs showing the highest allowed speed. Which word means 'speed limit'?
The train drivers refuse to work for a day because they want more pay, so no trains run.
The workers at a factory all stop working together to ask for better conditions. What are they doing?
Teachers stand outside the school with signs instead of giving lessons. Which verb means 'to strike'?

en: so far, until now, up to now
situations: You are at page 100 of a 300-page book. A friend asks if it is good, and you say you have liked everything you read up to this moment.
You have lived in a new city for three months, and up to this point nothing bad has happened. Which adverb do you use?
Your teacher asks how many words you have learned until this moment. Which word means 'so far'?
You want to travel to a country that requires an official permit in your passport before you arrive. You go to the embassy to get it.
At the border the officer asks for your passport and the official permission that lets you stay in the country for 30 days.
Before a trip to the USA you check which document besides your passport you must apply for. Which word means 'visa'?
Your hotel is in the middle of the city, close to the main square and all the shops.
The main station is in the middle of town, so it is easy to reach from everywhere. How do you describe its position?
A teacher says the most important idea of the story is its main point. Which adjective means 'central'?
At Easter children look for chocolate figures of a long-eared animal that is said to bring colourful eggs.
In a field a wild brown animal with very long ears jumps fast away as you come close.
In an old story a very fast animal with long ears loses a race to a slow one. Which word means 'hare'?
At work you stand in front of your team with slides and show the results of your project.
At university each student must show their topic to the class for ten minutes using a screen.
A company shows its new car to the press for the first time at a big event. Which verb means 'to present'?
You wrap your sandwich in a thin shiny silver sheet to keep it fresh.
In the meeting room the teacher puts a clear sheet on the overhead projector and writes on it.
The new phone has a thin plastic layer on the screen that you peel off first. Which word means 'film' or 'foil'?
A toddler sits on the floor and plays with blocks, a little car and a teddy bear.
You tidy up the children's room and put the cars, dolls and puzzles back into the big box.
For your friend's daughter's birthday you look for a doll or a small train in a shop. What kind of thing is it? Which word means 'toy'?

en: to record, to include, to absorb, to accommodate
situations: You press the red button on your phone so that your voice and your song are saved and you can listen to them later.
A hotel has enough free rooms to take in another big group of guests tonight.
The editor decides to add your short story to the new book, so the book will now have it too. Which verb means 'to include'?
You apply for a job. Together with your letter you must send a page listing your schools, jobs and skills.
The manager reads a document that shows your education and work history in order by date.
Before an interview you prepare the one-page paper with all your past schools and jobs. Which word means 'CV'?
You take a bag from a shop without paying. The police say this is an act that the law punishes.
A lawyer explains that driving without a licence is something for which you can be taken to court.
Your friend asks if copying a film illegally is allowed. You say no, you could be prosecuted. Which adjective means 'punishable'?
The shoes you bought are too small. You go back to the shop with the receipt and get a bigger size instead.
A sign in a shop says that within 14 days you may bring an item back and take a different one in its place.
You received a shirt as a gift in the wrong colour. At the customer service desk you swap it for another. Which word means 'exchange'?
At the post office the clerk presses a small tool with ink onto your letter to mark the date.
At the office you press a rubber tool on a paper to mark it as received, and the company name appears in ink.
At the border an officer puts an ink mark in your passport that shows the date you entered. Which word means 'stamp'?
Your old car needs 10 litres of petrol for every 100 kilometres. It really uses a lot.
At the end of the month the family has finished all the milk and rice; nothing is left.
An old fridge takes lots of electricity every year. Which verb means 'to consume'?
On a cold morning you cannot see the end of the street, and the cars drive slowly with their lights on.
Over the river a thick white cloud lies close to the ground, so you cannot see the other bank.
The weather report warns about low visibility on the roads because of white mist. Which word means 'fog'?
The shop does not have the red bag you wanted. The seller shows you a different option you could take instead.
The main road is closed, so you look on your phone for a second route to use instead.
Your doctor says the first medicine does not work, so he suggests a different one that can take its place. Which adjective describes this other choice?
In a big company, you work in the group of people who handle only money matters, with its own boss.
In a hospital, you go to the section that treats only children.
In a big store, the clothes, toys and food are in separate parts on different floors. Which word means 'department'?

en: just as, as much as, as well, equally, likewise
situations: Your colleague says 'Have a nice weekend!' and you want to wish him the same in return. Which word means 'likewise'?
Anna is tall. Her brother is exactly the same height. How do you say he is tall 'just as' much?
You need to buy bread, and you need milk too. Which word means 'as well'?
Before your sister's birthday you put her present in the wardrobe so she cannot find it.
In a game with children, you go behind the curtain so that the others do not see you.
A dog digs a hole in the garden and puts its bone in it so nobody finds it. Which verb means 'to hide'?
At the market you buy a small, soft, orange-yellow summer fruit with one stone inside, a bit like a small peach.
Your breakfast yogurt has pieces of a small, orange, velvety fruit in it.
The seller at the fruit stall holds up a small orange fruit that grows on trees in summer. Which word means 'apricot'?
Your baby makes a first small move on his own feet and you clap.
Your doctor says you should walk ten thousand of these every day, and your phone counts them.
The teacher explains how to solve the task: first stage one, then stage two. Which word means 'step'?
In the film, the two lovers meet in the rain at the station. This short part of the film is the one you remember best.
At the theatre rehearsal the director says: let's do the part where the king enters again, from the start.
A man shouts loudly at a cashier and everyone stares at him. Your friend says he made a public fuss. Which word means 'scene'?

en: to handle, to complete, to do, to deal with, to take care of
situations: You have a list: buy stamps, pay the bill, call the doctor. At the end of the day you have done all these tasks.
Your boss asks if the report is ready, and you say you will take care of it today.
Before the holidays you go through your small jobs one by one and tick them off. Which verb means 'to take care of'?
Hamburg lies at the top of Germany on the map, far away from the Alps.
On a compass the needle points to the direction opposite south, and a cold wind comes from that side.
Sweden is in the upper part of Europe. Which adjective describes its position, 'northern'?
After the main course the waiter asks if you want something sweet, like ice cream or cake, to finish your meal.
At home your mother cooks pasta and then brings out chocolate pudding at the end of the meal.
On a restaurant menu, after the starters and the main dishes comes the last section with sweet items. What is this section called?
At the zoo you see a slow animal with a hard round shell on its back that pulls its head inside.
While swimming in the sea you see a big animal with a shell and flippers. Later it crawls onto the beach to lay eggs.
Your friend keeps a small pet with a shell in a glass tank and feeds it lettuce. Which word means 'turtle' or 'tortoise'?

en: to get used to, to become accustomed, to accustom
situations: You moved to a new country and at first the cold weather was hard, but after a few months it feels normal to you.
Your new shoes hurt at first, but slowly your feet become used to them.
A baby cries in his new bed at first, but after a week he accepts it as normal. Which verb means 'to get used to'?
The doctor puts a cold stethoscope on the front upper part of your body to listen to your heart.
You do push-ups and train the muscles on the front of your upper body.
At the butcher you ask for the white meat from the front part of the chicken. Which word means 'breast'?
A man who stole a lot is locked away for two years behind bars, in a building with guards.
In a film the thief escapes from the place where criminals serve their sentence.
You walk past a big building with high walls and barbed wire where convicted people live. Which word means 'prison'?
An advert says 'Meet your ... neighbours!' about people who will move into the new building next year.
The city plans how streets should look in the year 2050, for time that has not come yet. Which adjective describes these plans?
Your friend introduces the man she will marry next month as her ... husband, because he is not yet her husband. Which adjective means 'future'?

en: to detect, to determine, to find out, to notice, to realize
situations: At home you count your money and notice that 20 euros are missing from your wallet.
A doctor does some tests and finds out what illness you have.
The mechanic checks your car and discovers that the brakes are broken. Which verb means 'to find out'?
A form has a box where you must write the name of the town where you live, not your street. What is this box called?
Your bank asks you to tell them if the city where you live changes after you move.
A job advert says the employee's home town must be near the office. Which word means 'place of residence'?
At a dinner invitation, the host brings out a sweet course after the main meal, and everyone says it was the best part.
In the school canteen you get a small fruit yogurt after your lunch as the sweet last course.
At your birthday party the guests finish the main food, then you serve the cake as the sweet course. Which word means that last sweet course?
Two friends first sat close together; now they sit far from each other at opposite ends of the table. Which word describes the distance?
The old book is falling into separate pieces, because the pages are coming away from each other.
Two twins grow up in different cities and live far away from one another. Which adverb means 'apart'?
At the theatre the curtain opens and the actors walk onto the raised platform in front of the audience.
At a rock concert the singer jumps up onto the raised platform where the band plays.
In your school play you wait behind the curtain before you go out in front of everyone. Which word means 'stage'?
Smoking is not good for your lungs; it does something bad to your health.
Too much sugar can hurt your teeth over many years.
A doctor says one glass of wine will not do you any harm. Which verb means 'to harm'?
The winter was warm and soft, so you only need a light jacket in January.
The judge gives a young man who made a small mistake a punishment that is not hard.
The doctor gives you a soap with a gentle formula that does not hurt your skin. Which adjective means 'gentle'?
In a film a man saves the children from a burning house and everyone cheers for him. What is he called?
A boy dreams of becoming a brave man who saves the world, like the ones in his comic books.
In a fairy tale a young brave man fights the dragon and rescues the princess. Which word means 'hero'?
You want to hang a picture on the wall. You need a tool to knock the nail into it.
A carpenter hits nails into wood with a heavy tool that has a metal head and a wooden handle.
In your toolbox you find pliers, a screwdriver and a heavy tool with a metal head for knocking nails. Which word names this missing tool?
You secretly plan a party for your friend and want her to be happily shocked when she opens the door.
Your husband brings you flowers for no reason. You did not expect it, and he did it to make you glad.
The test result is much better than you expected and you can hardly believe it. Which verb means 'to surprise'?
In the cinema your ticket says row 5, place 12. What is the thing you sit on called?
The company has its main office in Frankfurt, where the managers work. What is this place called?
You buy new trousers and check the way they sit on your body, not too tight, not too loose. Which word means 'fit'?
For breakfast you spread a sweet fruit spread from a glass jar onto your bread.
Your grandmother cooks plums with sugar in a big pot and fills small glasses with the sweet spread.
On a shop shelf there are glasses of strawberry, cherry and orange spread to put on toast. Which word means 'jam'?
Your teenage son comes home late and sneaks in quietly so that his parents do not hear him.
Two friends meet in a quiet corner and tell each other something nobody else may know.
A cat walks slowly and quietly toward a bird without being noticed. Which word means 'stealthy' or 'secret'?
You open a big box and look at what is inside it.
The teacher asks you to say in a few sentences what the story is about.
A list on the bottle tells you what is in it: water, sugar and lemon. Which word means 'contents'?
It is snowing heavily, so the organisers decide the football match will not take place.
You are sick and call your friend to say you cannot come to his party after all, even though you had agreed.
The company tells the singer to stop the concert planned for Friday because of the storm. Which verb means 'to cancel'?
In class the students talk about school uniforms and each one gives an opinion, with arguments for and against.
At dinner your family talks for an hour about where to go on holiday, with many different opinions.
A radio programme has guests who exchange arguments about a topic. Which word means 'discussion'?
A tanker travels through a large bay of the sea between Iran and Saudi Arabia.
On the map of Mexico, you see the big curve of sea to the east of Texas and Florida.
A geography teacher points to a large part of the sea that cuts deep into the land. Which word means 'gulf'?

en: to think, to think about, to reflect, to ponder, to contemplate
situations: Your boss asks you to join a new project. You say you need two days to think carefully before you answer.
In the exam you sit silently with your pen in your hand, thinking hard about the answer.
A friend asks whether you will move abroad. You say you will consider it. Which verb means 'to ponder'?
You write down your doctor's appointment, your meeting and your friend's party in a small book that you carry around.
On your phone you have an app that lists all your meetings by day and time.
Your boss says: look in your planner, are you free on Tuesday? Which word means 'planner' or 'diary'?
You find a wallet with 100 euros and bring it to the police without taking anything. People say you tell the truth and do not steal.
Your friend asks how his new haircut looks. You say what you really think, even if it is not nice.
A cashier gives you too much change and you give it back. Which adjective describes you, 'honest'?
In a race you are in front of all the other runners; the others are behind you.
You go to the restaurant first to get a table, while your family comes later. You go before them.
A friend walks faster and is a few metres in front. You call 'Go on, I will follow!' Which adverb means 'ahead'?
In autumn the farmer collects potatoes and wheat from the fields after a long summer.
After heavy rain this year, the apple trees gave few fruits. Farmers complain that what they gathered is small.
Villagers celebrate a festival to give thanks for the gathering of the crops. Which word means 'harvest'?

en: to grow, to increase, to wax
situations: Your little son gets taller every year, and his trousers are too short again.
You plant a seed in a pot and every week the plant gets bigger.
The number of people living in the city goes up each year. Which verb means 'to grow' or 'to increase'?
Your company sends you to a two-day course to learn new software skills for your job.
A teacher goes to a seminar in the holidays to learn new methods for her lessons.
A nurse takes evening classes to improve her professional skills. Which word means 'further training'?
Your sister has a baby girl. What is the baby to you?
At the family party, your brother's six-year-old daughter gives you a drawing. Who is she to you?
Your uncle talks proudly about his brother's daughter. What is she to him? Which word means 'niece'?
On a clear day you can see the mountain from far away because nothing blocks the view.
A reflective vest makes a cyclist easy to see at night.
A message written with special ink shows nothing, until you hold it under a lamp and it appears. Which adjective means 'visible'?
In the zoo a long thin animal without legs slides across the ground and hisses.
At the supermarket many people wait one behind the other at the till. You stand at the end of it.
On a hike your guide warns you to be careful in the grass because a long legless animal with a bite may be there. Which word means 'snake'?

en: to read, to read aloud, to read out
situations: At bedtime your child asks you to say the words of a picture book out loud while she listens.
In class the teacher asks you to say the text in your book out loud for everybody.
Your grandfather cannot see well, so you speak the words from the newspaper aloud for him. Which verb means 'to read aloud'?
You feel tired and weak this morning, with no strength to do anything.
Your electricity bill is high, so the company that supplies power to your flat sends you a letter.
Wind and sun can produce clean power for homes. Which word means 'energy'?
